messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 — inference-service-high-error-rate fired for service `inference-dedicated-eu`. Incident: INC12345. Symptoms: elevated 5xx (502/503) and kernel compile failures on dedicated GPU pool. Pager: @kai (oncall)

Kai Liao: Acked in PD, I'm taking first triage. Pulling relevant logs and checking autoscaler events.

Kai Liao: Quick status — 95th latency > 2s, error-rate ~12% across dedicated-eu. Noticed a burst of model compile errors right before nodes crash.

Priya Shah: I can jump in for infra rollback if needed. If it's a runtime/kernel regression we should consider reverting the recent runtime build.

IncidentBot: Auto-escalation: because of repeated reassign requests, paging Nate O'Connor as secondary.

Nate O'Connor: Taking ownership for now. Kai — please handoff initial findings. I'll coordinate rollback if confirmed.

Kai Liao: Handoff notes: logs show compile OOMs and immediate node exit after new runtime r-infer-478 deployed ~09:57Z. Log sample:
```
2026-03-17T09:58:12Z ERROR compile_kernel: OOM allocating workspace
model=fast-13b quant=8bit variant=redwood/fast-13b
node=gpu-dedicated-eu-3 runtime=r-infer-478
stack: nv_compiler.cc:142
```
Autoscaler then created replacement nodes which also failed. Also seeing many warnings referencing cudnn driver 8.2.4.

Priya Shah: Interesting — our canary had r-infer-478 but it passed CI. Possible driver/runtime mismatch on dedicated pool nodes. I can prepare rollback PR to r-infer-476 and pin cudnn to 8.2.2 for dedicated-eu.

Customer Success: CS note: Multiple customers (CUST-2143, CUST-2201) reporting 502s for inference in EU; one is on Dedicated. We're drafting an outbound.

Mike Rhoades: Opening incident bridge and runbook link: https://meet/bridge/INC12345 | runbook: https://docs.internal/runbooks/compile-oom. Adding monitoring hooks.

Nate O'Connor: Plan: 1) rollback runtime on a canary subset of dedicated-eu nodes 2) validate canary 3) roll to remainder in waves 4) monitor error-rate & latency. Priya, want you to apply rollback; Kai will monitor model worker logs. Mike, please coordinate CS outbound.

Priya Shah: Preparing rollback change now, will patch canary first. ETA ~10m.

Kai Liao: Noted an additional signal — kernel module load errors referencing cudnn mismatch when container requests GPU compute. Might explain why only dedicated pool affected (custom host driver).

Priya Shah: Canary rollback to r-infer-476 applied at 10:07Z. Monitoring canary metrics.

IncidentBot: Bridge created by Mike Rhoades: https://meet/bridge/INC12345

Priya Shah: Canary healthy after rollback — error-rate back to baseline (0 -> 0.5%) and latency restored. :white_check_mark:

Mike Rhoades: Observing error-rate across canary nodes drop from ~12% -> 1.5% over 3m. CS: are you sending customer update?

Customer Success: Outbound sent to impacted customers: brief explanation and ETA for full remediation. Will follow up when we complete roll.

Nate O'Connor: Rolling rollback to remainder of dedicated-eu pool in waves now. Will monitor each wave.

Kai Liao: Confirming kernel warnings clear on canary after rollback, no further OOM traces.

Priya Shah: Rollout at 60% completed, error rate continues trending down.

Mike Rhoades: Metrics: global 5xx from 12% -> 0.9% after 30m. Canary and waves look healthy.

Nate O'Connor: Full roll complete at 10:23Z. Error rates at baseline. Closing PD and bridge. Postmortem to follow; Kai to own.

Customer Success: Customers notified that service is restored and CS will coordinate any additional remediation with engineering.

Kai Liao: Postmortem action items (initial): 1) investigate r-infer-478 runtime build and regression tests, 2) add CI integration to detect cudnn/driver mismatch on dedicated host images, 3) pin driver for dedicated pools until validated.

Priya Shah: Creating infra ticket for driver pinning and deployment gating.

Mike Rhoades: Thanks for quick ops. Closing bridge.

IncidentBot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 resolved by Nate O'Connor at 2026-03-17T10:23:47Z

Kai Liao: I'll draft the postmortem and include logs and timeline. Assigning follow-ups: kernel pin (Priya), CI gating (Kai), customer follow-up (CS).

Mike Rhoades: :thumbsup: Great work team — nice and surgical rollback.
